newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina mortgage bank sale delayed after brawl.
newsitem.headline: Argentina mortgage bank sale delayed after brawl.

text.p: A debate in Argentina's Congress on the privatiztion of state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario Nacional has been postponed until next week after it broke into a brawl, Congress officials said Wednesday.
The row erupted late Tuesday as Mary Sanchez, a deputy from the opposition centre-left Frepaso alliance made history by becoming the first woman to hit a man in parliament.
Sanchez told local television Wednesday that she slapped Peronist Party whip Jorge Matzkin in the face after he cursed her.
That led to a brief scuffle as opposition politicians rushed around Sanchez to defend her from angry Peronists.
Tempers were running high already as the opposition accused the Peronists of "authoritarianism" for insisting on waiting hours for a quorum to be reached in the chamber.
But when a quorum was reached, allowing the debate and vote on the issue to follow, deputies started leaving the chamber and the session ended without completing business.
Matzkin denied Wednesday he had cursed at Sanchez.
"No way, I do not insult women, and much less within the political field," he told reporters.

Since President Carlos Menem came to power in 1989, the country has seen mass privatizations of everything from the railways, water works and utility companies to the imminent sale of the post office and airports.
Opponents fear Hipotecario's privatization could end the bank's role in providing accessible home loans.

Those criticisms have led the government to write into the draft privatization bill the promise that some of the $2.5-3.0 billion expected revenue will be used to finance public works, including credits to build new housing.

That led former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo to charge last week that use of the proceeds of the sale for public works would be a "grave error...with clearly electoral aims," in reference to mid-term Congress elections in October.
Cavallo argues the revenues should rather be used to reduce Argentina's growing public debt.

The Finance and Budget Committee of the lower house of Congress has approved the sale of the bank, but insists that Hipotecario's home lending role all over Argentina, even in small towns and villages, be maintained for at least 10 years.
Hipotecario is Argentina's largest bank in terms of assets, which are valued at $4.31 billion.
